growth_story.headline: Income per person in the West Bank and Gaza rose from 2003 to a 2016 peak, then stalled and collapsed in war; in 2025 it was near its 1997 level.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in the West Bank and Gaza has moved through three eras since 1995, each shaped more by conflict and limits on movement than by ordinary business cycles. From 1995 to 2002 it fell 1.4 percent a year on average: gains in the late 1990s were wiped out when closures during the second intifada cut trade and jobs. From 2003 to 2016 it grew 4.8 percent a year, starting with a sharp rebound and then slower growth driven by spending in the West Bank, while Gaza fell behind under the blockade imposed in 2007. After the 2016 peak, income per person shrank 4.1 percent a year from 2017 to 2025: it slipped as donor support fell and tax transfers were disputed, dropped in the 2020 pandemic, and collapsed in 2024 during the war centered in Gaza. In 2025 it was 33.9 percent below the 2016 peak, about where it first stood in 1997.

threads.title: Intifada and closures
threads.text: Income per person rose in the late 1990s, then fell in each year from 2000 to 2002, by 10.9, 11.6 and 14.7 percent. The World Bank traced the crisis to closures: Israeli limits on moving goods and people across borders and inside the territories during the second intifada.

threads.title: Blockade splits Gaza off
threads.text: After 2007 the two territories went separate ways. Under the blockade and repeated wars, income per person in Gaza declined on average, while the West Bank kept growing. The combined figures for the 2003 to 2016 era hide this split.

threads.title: Spending-led growth loses support
threads.text: Growth leaned on household and government spending rather than on producing goods. Budget support from donors shrank fast after 2014, and in 2019 a standoff arose over the tax revenues Israel collects for the Palestinian Authority. Income per person fell in each year from 2017 to 2019.

threads.title: War since October 2023
threads.text: The war that began in October 2023 brought Gaza's economy to a standstill and cut most of the jobs Palestinians held in Israel. Income per person fell 24.7 percent in 2024, the largest drop in the series. It grew 1.9 percent in 2025, a recovery the World Bank calls uneven.

since_last_year.text: Tax revenue transfers from Israel have been fully suspended since May 2025. The October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza opened a fragile window for stabilization, and income per person grew 1.9 percent in 2025, an uneven recovery from the 2024 collapse. In early 2026 the Palestinian Authority borrowed more from domestic banks.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank says total output had fallen back to its 2009 level by the end of 2024. Income per person fell further than that: by 2025 it was about where it first stood in 1997, because the population kept growing. The World Bank also describes modest growth between 2010 and 2019, but in the data income per person was already falling slightly in each year from 2017 to 2019.
